about.what: Engine E3's settings and costs: Prairie City's energy hub (the three districts behind their substation limits) as a linear program over prairie-city.json's eight representative days. Prairie City's own numbers are in prairie-city.json; this file holds only what the engine adds.
about.line: Prairie City is fictional; its numbers are illustrative.
about.builtBy: Written by the engine E3 data build step (do not edit by hand); the `precomputed` block is written by the tests' --write mode
about.set: Costs read from other course files say so in `via`; everything marked "teaching" is illustrative, set for this course, with a range the reader can change.

finance.note: Every up-front cost is paid as a yearly amount: the up-front cost x the capital recovery factor at a 4% real rate over the item's life, plus its upkeep. 4% real is lesson 13's rate (a round value inside the 2025 ATB's financing range).

heatPump.note: EIA's minimum-efficiency air-source heat pump, installed, per home ($6,730 in 2022 dollars, x 1.0928 to 2025 dollars with EIA's GDP deflator, as engine E0 does); 15-year life. Its efficiency through the year is Prairie City's COP curve (prairie-city.json, cop), not this unit's rating. Commercial buildings are counted as home-equivalents by their heat need.

retrofit.note: Set for teaching: an envelope package (air sealing, attic and wall insulation, duct sealing) that cuts a home's space-heat need by the share you set, at a cost per home you set (2025 dollars), lasting 30 years. For scale: ORNL's national evaluation of DOE's Weatherization Assistance Program found that gas-heated single-family homes weatherized in program year 2008 cut their gas use by 17.8%, at an average cost of $4,695 a home in 2008 dollars (not converted here).

dh.note: Set for teaching: a hot-water network in the dense core; each connected home-equivalent costs the network sum you set (pipes and connections, 40 years); 10% of the heat sent out is lost in the pipes. The plant is a large electric heat pump on a steady heat source (COP 3.0 every hour, fed through the core's substation; cost per kW of heat, 25 years) with a gas boiler (90%) for the rest, which is assumed to exist already and is counted at its fuel only. The store is a water tank: cost per MWh of heat it holds (30 years), 0.5% of its heat lost each hour, filled or emptied in 4 hours or more.

ev.note: Managed charging moves each day's charging energy to any hour of the same day, at most one sixth of it in one hour (a day's charge takes 6 hours or more): it assumes cars can plug in at home or at work. Unmanaged charging follows prairie-city.json's evening profile. Vehicles' prices are outside the boundary: only their fuel and electricity are counted.

rooftop.note: EIA's residential solar system, installed, per kW ($4,336 in 2022 dollars, x 1.0928 to 2025 dollars, as engine E0 does); upkeep $20 per kW a year (illustrative, E0's); 25-year life. Output per MW follows prairie-city.json's solar shape on each day, scaled to EIA's 17.6% rooftop capacity factor.

battery.note: Neighbourhood batteries at the substations, 4 hours: NREL's 2024 cost ($372 per kW plus $241 per kWh, 2024 dollars, x 1.0263 to 2025 dollars with BEA's deflator, as capstone C2 does), 4% of it a year of upkeep, 15 years; 85% of a charge comes back (the loss is taken on charging).

upgrade.note: Set for teaching: more room at a district's substation (a transformer and feeders), an up-front cost per kW you set, paid over 40 years. The model buys only what the busiest hour needs after every flexible load has moved.

tie.note: Stated small costs, far below any real one, that pick one plan when several cost the same: $20 a year per MW of each district's busiest hour, $10 per MW of the three districts' busiest hour together, $1 per MWh out of a battery, $0.50 per MWh out of the heat store, and $0.10 per MWh of managed charging times the hour's share of SPP's peak demand (charging prefers quieter hours). They are left out of every reported cost.

indHP.note: Set for teaching: industrial heat pumps for the food plants' heat below 100 C (washing, pasteurizing, hot water), COP 3.0, $900 per kW of heat, 20 years, running flat all year.

avoided.note: Set for teaching: what one MWh from the wind contract or the solar farm saves the city's supplier when it replaces a bought MWh; the wires part of the bill is still paid.

gasInd.note: Set for teaching: the range C3's sensitivity test moves the industrial park's gas price over (prairie-city.json prices.gasPerMcf.industrial, itself set for teaching from EIA's Kansas citygate price); not a forecast.

c3.note: C3 plans Prairie City for 2040 with 2025's people, homes and prices and the course's synthetic weather: only the plan changes. The industrial park and the data-center campus take power at their own substations (no limit modelled); the park's new loads are flat all year.

fullYear.note: The full-year check re-runs a plan on every hour of 2025 with the same LP and constraints, keeping what the eight days decided: the building shares, the sizes and each district's substation upgrade. Load a substation cannot carry is left unserved at $10,000 per MWh (lesson 13's illustrative penalty), never part of a reported cost. 2025 as it is is re-run the same way, so each change against 2025 is like for like.

c3ex.title: Two summaries of the same brief
c3ex.task: Recommend Prairie City's 2040 energy plan within the budget, and say who gains and who pays.

parts.text: go green with heat pumps and wind
parts.note: No sizes, no shares, no budget: the council cannot check or cost it.
By how much, on what boundary, against which year?
Who? The household table is a screening estimate with an adoption rule; name the groups and the numbers.

parts.text: Some people objected but the plan is the best
parts.note: Each objection needs an answer: what you would change, or why you would not.

parts.text: switch 70% of furnaces and resistance heat to heat pumps, retrofit 10% of buildings, make 40% of cars electric with managed charging, add 30 MW of substation batteries, move the food plants' low-temperature heat to heat pumps, and contract 200 MW of wind and a 100 MW solar farm at site A
parts.note: Every lever with its size: a plan the council can cost and check.

parts.text: $1,227.9M up front against $1,500.0M; the city's yearly cost −$28.9M against 2025 (energy bills plus equipment as yearly payments, 2025 dollars)
parts.note: Up front and yearly kept apart, on one boundary.

parts.text: the city's location-based CO₂ 2,423,488 t a year, 12% below 2025 (operating only; the contracts not deducted); 26 MW of substation upgrades, the suburbs the tightest
parts.note: The cut with its boundary, and where the plan needs grid room.

parts.text: energy burden of homes below 80% of area median income 6.1% → 5.5%, every group adopting alike; the cars' fuel and charging count as transport, outside the burden
parts.note: The rule stated, and the estimate labelled as a screening estimate.

parts.text: about 2,947 construction job-years to 2040 (gross), 2,358 net of displacement; at the farms 18 direct ongoing jobs, 29 gross supported, 23 net of displacement
parts.note: Job-years kept apart from ongoing jobs, gross apart from net.

parts.text: site A, the best of A19's five blocks and the cheapest to connect ($5.3M), at a 23.8% capacity factor
parts.note: The site's choice with its evidence from the map.

parts.text: the yearly cost runs from −$72.3M to −$2.6M with every input at its lower- or higher-cost end; value of a contract MWh moves it most, $20/MWh to $80/MWh; every tested input is set for teaching
parts.note: A range, the input that matters most, and what kind of number each input is.

parts.text: to the electric utility (26 MW of upgrades): I keep them, since with the plan's levers fixed they are the cheapest way to meet the suburbs' busiest hour (its dual equals the upgrade's yearly cost); to the climate group (12% cut): the wind and solar contracts do not lower the location-based CO₂ (a market-based report could claim about 301,316 t); deeper cuts need more heat pumps and retrofits, with $272.1M of the budget left; to the industrial park (+$2.2M a year, 7%): I keep the food plants' heat pumps for the gas they save, and show the park's gas price in the sensitivity table; to farmers and rural residents (site A): it is the screen's best block and the cheapest of the five to connect, $5.3M for its line, road and land, 1.0 km to S4, on about 542 acres
parts.note: Each objection answered with a reason or a change, from the run's own numbers.

parts.text: 2025's people and prices held to 2040, one substation per district, eight representative days of synthetic weather (on all 8,760 hours the upgrades fall 5.7 MW short, on 19 Feb and 20 Feb), the household rule an assumption, the map's layers simulated
parts.note: What the plan leaves out, and what the full-year check found, so the council does not over-read it.

c3ex.note: Both summaries are illustrative. The strong one quotes this engine's numbers for one reference plan within the budget, precomputed; another plan is just as strong when its evidence supports it.
